exec: Italy is treating recent disruption as a hybrid-threat campaign, and cybersecurity funding is now a live budget issue.
plain: Italy's prime minister briefed opposition parties on a run of hoax threats and cyberattacks and asked for political unity. How much the budget gives to cybersecurity is still being debated.
summary: After bomb-threat emails reached Italian schools, with one wave reported at 1,803 institutions, and earlier tampering with supermarket freezers, Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni held a majority summit and then invited opposition parties to a briefing. Foreign Minister Tajani linked the threats to Italy's support for Ukraine; Deputy PM Salvini was more cautious. Opposition parties criticised last year's cut to the national cybersecurity strategy fund.
title: Italy's Meloni briefs opposition on hybrid threats after school and supermarket attacks

validation.note: Two articles from the same Italian weekly; no attribution has been officially confirmed.
